name: Composio
tagline: Hosted tool and MCP platform that connects agents to 1,700+ apps with managed per-user authentication.
bestFor: Developers adding many SaaS integrations to their own agents
description: Composio hosts tools for 1,700+ apps and generates per-user MCP URLs, handling each user's OAuth connections and letting you restrict which tools a server exposes. A free plan includes 10,000 tool calls per month, and the Standard plan costs $18 per seat per month.
pros: Free plan includes 10,000 tool calls per month and up to 3 members
1,700+ apps available on every plan
allowed_tools setting limits which tools each MCP server exposes
Extra tool calls on Standard cost $0.005 each
cons: Audit logs, SCIM and SIEM streaming are Enterprise-only
No annual price listed
Free plan has no Firewall or SSO and stops at 10,000 tool calls
freePlanDetails: 10,000 tool calls per month, $2 one-time credits, up to 3 members, up to 3 custom MCP servers, 5 connections and 25 skills; no credit card required.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: 10,000 tool calls per month; app tool calls stop at the limit; $2 one-time credits; up to 3 members.

plans.name: Standard
plans.notes: Per seat per month. 10,000 tool calls per seat per month, pooled across the workspace, plus $18 credits per seat. Extra tool calls $0.005 each; Firewall policies $0.50 per 1M tokens. Includes SSO and zero data retention.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Volume pricing. Bring your own cloud, custom connectors, SCIM, audit logs, SIEM streaming, dedicated Slack channel and SLAs. IT admin seats are free.

name: Mintive (formerly MintMCP)
tagline: Managed MCP gateway that hosts connectors and adds SSO, per-user credentials and audit logs.
bestFor: Companies rolling out MCP servers to many employees
description: Mintive, renamed from MintMCP in October 2026, runs MCP connectors in its own cloud and exposes them to clients such as ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor with per-user OAuth tokens, access policies and audit logs. Pricing is not published; it is quoted per user plus a platform fee.
pros: 1,000+ pre-built connectors
Records every tool call with user, timestamp and optional payload
Per-user OAuth tokens stored encrypted and refreshed automatically
SOC 2 Type II audited
cons: No public prices or free plan
Only a managed cloud deployment is listed
Renamed in October 2026, so some pages still use the MintMCP name

plans.name: Custom
plans.notes: Per-user licensing plus platform fees; quoted by team size (1-100, 101-1,000, 1,001-9,999 and 10,000+ users).

name: Docker MCP Gateway
tagline: Open-source Docker CLI plugin that runs MCP servers in containers behind one gateway.
bestFor: Developers running local MCP servers in isolated containers
description: Docker MCP Gateway is the MIT-licensed engine behind the MCP Toolkit in Docker Desktop: it runs each MCP server in its own container, injects secrets, handles OAuth flows and lets you enable or disable individual tools per profile. The gateway is free; a managed governance offering is invite-only through Docker Sales.
pros: MIT license, 1,600+ GitHub stars
Docker MCP Catalog lists 300+ servers; Docker builds and signs the local ones
Per-profile tool allowlists (enable or disable single tools)
Runs over stdio, SSE or streaming HTTP on a chosen port
cons: Mainly a single-machine developer tool; team access control is not documented in the open-source gateway
Profiles and secrets features rely on Docker Desktop 4.59+ by default
Docker AI Governance (central management) is invite-only
freePlanDetails: Open-source gateway (MIT); included with the MCP Toolkit in Docker Desktop.

plans.name: Open source
plans.notes: MIT-licensed docker-mcp CLI plugin; works in Docker Desktop or standalone.

plans.name: Docker AI Governance
plans.notes: Invite-only; contact Docker Sales. Price not published.

integrations: 300+ MCP servers in the Docker MCP Catalog

name: Obot
tagline: Open-source MCP gateway, server host and registry with identity-based access control and audit logs.
bestFor: IT teams that want a self-hosted MCP control plane
description: Obot is an MIT-licensed platform that hosts MCP servers in Docker or Kubernetes, combines them into virtual MCP endpoints, manages OAuth and shared credentials, and controls server and tool access by user or identity-provider group. The self-hosted Community edition is free for up to 100 users; Obot Cloud and Enterprise prices are not published.
pros: MIT license; Community edition free for up to 100 users
Virtual MCP servers combine several servers behind one endpoint with per-group tool access
Turns any OpenAPI-described HTTP API into a hosted MCP server
SCIM provisioning from Okta and correlated audit logs
cons: Obot Cloud and Enterprise prices are not published
Enterprise auth providers in Community require registration
Device management (Obot Sentry) is still in beta
freePlanDetails: Obot Community: open source, self-hosted, up to 100 users and 100 Sentry devices.

plans.name: Community
plans.notes: Open source (MIT), self-hosted; up to 100 users and 100 Sentry devices.

plans.name: Obot Cloud
plans.notes: Hosted, dedicated control plane; enterprise SSO/OIDC, no user limit. Price not published; 7-day free trial.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Self-hosted; unlimited users and devices, enterprise support. Contact sales.

name: TrueFoundry MCP Gateway
tagline: MCP gateway bundled with an LLM gateway, with per-user OAuth, per-tool RBAC and audit logs.
bestFor: Teams that want LLM and MCP traffic governed in one gateway
description: TrueFoundry's AI Gateway includes an MCP gateway that stores and refreshes each user's OAuth tokens, enforces per-server and per-tool permissions, and lets virtual MCP servers expose a subset of tools to chosen users or teams. The Developer plan is free for up to 3 users and Pro costs $25 per user per month.
pros: Free Developer plan for up to 3 users, with 5 MCP servers and 10K gateway requests per user per month
Permissions per server and per tool, by user, team or virtual account
Deploys in VPC, on-prem or air-gapped (Enterprise)
SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA and GDPR listed in the Trust Center
cons: Developer and Pro run as SaaS only
MCP tool approvals are Enterprise-only
Pro charges $20 per additional 100K gateway requests above 20K per user
freePlanDetails: Developer plan: free for up to 3 users; 5 MCP servers, 1 virtual MCP, 5 model accounts, 10K gateway requests per user per month; no credit card.

plans.name: Developer
plans.notes: Free for up to 3 users; SaaS only; 5 MCP servers, 1 virtual MCP, 10K AI Gateway requests per user per month.

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: Per user per month, no minimum commitment; unlimited virtual MCPs; 20K requests per user per month, then $20 per additional 100K; SSO included; SaaS only. Model-provider costs billed separately without markup.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Annual commitment; MCP tool approvals, custom guardrails, VPC, on-prem or air-gapped deployment.

name: IBM ContextForge
tagline: Open-source registry and proxy that federates MCP, A2A and REST/gRPC services behind one endpoint.
bestFor: Platform teams self-hosting a federated MCP registry
description: ContextForge is an Apache-2.0 gateway from IBM that federates MCP servers, A2A agents and REST or gRPC APIs, bundles selected tools into virtual servers, and adds team-scoped RBAC and user-scoped OAuth tokens. It is free to self-host via PyPI, Docker or Kubernetes.
pros: Apache-2.0 license, about 4,800 GitHub stars
Converts REST and gRPC services into MCP tools
Team-scoped RBAC with a tools.execute permission
40+ plugins and OpenTelemetry tracing
cons: No paid support plan or hosted version listed
Production containers do not support arm64
Audit logging of individual tool calls is not clearly documented

plans.name: Open source
plans.notes: Apache-2.0; install from PyPI (mcp-contextforge-gateway), Docker image or Kubernetes/Helm.

compliance: SSO via Google, GitHub or Entra ID

name: Microsoft MCP Gateway
tagline: Open-source reverse proxy that deploys and routes MCP servers on Kubernetes with Entra ID authorization.
bestFor: Azure and Kubernetes teams hosting their own MCP servers
description: Microsoft MCP Gateway is an MIT-licensed reverse proxy and control plane that deploys MCP servers to Kubernetes, routes each request statelessly and checks Entra ID app roles for read and write access. It is free to self-host, with a one-click Azure deployment option.
pros: MIT license, about 900 GitHub stars
REST control plane to deploy, update and delete MCP servers
Entra ID roles control who can read or change each server and tool
One-click deploy to Azure
cons: Requires Kubernetes
Current version only works with MCP 2026-07-28 clients
No catalog of ready-made servers; you supply container images

plans.name: Open source
plans.notes: MIT-licensed; runs on your own Kubernetes cluster or Azure. Azure resource costs are separate.

name: Zapier MCP
tagline: Hosted MCP server that gives AI clients actions across Zapier's 9,000+ connected apps.
bestFor: Non-developers connecting AI assistants to business apps
description: Zapier MCP exposes actions from 9,000+ apps to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other clients over Streamable HTTP, with credentials kept in Zapier's managed connections and every action recorded in History. It is included in every Zapier plan, including Free (100 tasks per month), and each successful tool call uses two tasks.
pros: Included in every Zapier plan, including Free
9,000+ apps; failed tool calls do not use tasks
Every MCP action is recorded in Zapier History
Enterprise admins can set app-level and action-level access
cons: Each successful tool call uses two tasks, so the Free plan's 100 tasks cover 50 calls
Cloud only; MCP servers outside Zapier cannot be added
Admin controls (per-workspace enablement, action restrictions) are Enterprise features
freePlanDetails: Zapier Free plan: 100 tasks per month (50 MCP tool calls), 1 user.
trial: 14-day free trial of Professional, no credit card

name: Kong AI Gateway
tagline: API gateway with plugins that proxy MCP traffic, turn REST APIs into MCP tools and apply per-tool ACLs.
bestFor: Companies already running Kong for their APIs
description: Kong AI Gateway adds MCP support through plugins that convert REST APIs into MCP tools, validate MCP OAuth 2.0 tokens and enforce per-tool access rules with audit logging. Konnect Plus starts at $25 per month plus usage, but Kong's plugin docs list the MCP Proxy and MCP OAuth2 plugins as AI Gateway Enterprise features.
pros: Converts existing REST API paths into MCP tools
Per-tool ACLs since version 3.13, with allowed and denied attempts written to an audit log
Runs on-prem or in Konnect
30-day Plus trial, no credit card
cons: MCP Proxy and MCP OAuth2 plugins are documented as AI Gateway Enterprise-only
Plus pricing adds many usage meters (requests, control planes, APIs)
SSO, RBAC and audit logging in Konnect are Enterprise-only
trial: 30-day free trial of Konnect Plus, no credit card

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Billed annually; custom pricing. Required for AI MCP Proxy and AI MCP OAuth2 plugins per plugin docs; SSO, RBAC and audit logging.

name: Arcade
tagline: Tool runtime with MCP gateways that combine tools from several servers under per-user authorization.
bestFor: Agent developers who need tools that act as the signed-in user
description: Arcade hosts 8,000+ tools and lets you build MCP gateways that federate tools from several servers, choose exactly which tools each gateway exposes, and serve them at a Streamable HTTP URL with tokens scoped to the signed-in user. A free plan includes 2,000 tool calls per month, and the Team plan costs $25 per month plus $0.01 per tool call.
pros: Free plan includes 2,000 tool calls per month, no credit card
8,000+ pre-built tools
Each gateway exposes only the tools you select
Enterprise can run in your VPC or fully air-gapped
cons: SSO, RBAC and audit logs are Enterprise-only
Team plan bills every tool call at $0.01 on top of the $25 fee
No annual price listed
freePlanDetails: 2,000 tool calls per month on Arcade Cloud; community support on Discord and GitHub; no credit card.
